title: Stat Reference
subtitle: How every mod stat works and stacks

entries.title: General Rules
entries.summary: Read first: terms and stacking rules

blocks.text: <hl>Mods</hl> are upgrade cards: weapon mods go on a weapon, Warframe mods go on you. Each bonus line on a card is a <hl>stat</hl>. This category lists every stat by purpose, ready to look up.

rows: The percentage printed on the card: +30% is written <t>0.3</t> in formulas
The same stat from every mod on one weapon (or one Warframe loadout) is <g>simply added</g>, then applied once
[[start/glossary|Riven mods]] (mods with random stats) can carry negative values that subtract from the total; a negative total works in reverse
The exception: the four Warframe resistances and {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryDelay} multiply card by card - see their entries

blocks.title: Mod rank
blocks.text: A mod below max rank applies <t>current rank ÷ {cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel}</t> of its stats. The numbers on the card are already scaled, so what you see is what you get. Ranking up: [[modules/module_level]].

blocks.title: Card values
blocks.text: Every mod applies the full values printed on its card.
Stats that only count whole 10% steps
These stats <w>only count whole 10% steps</w> and drop the remainder: 25% counts as 20%, 9% does nothing. Round your builds up to full steps.

items: {lang:item.module.attackSpeed}
{lang:item.module.attackRange} (each step adds only 5% reach)
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.health}
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.armor}
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.sprintSpeed}
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.knockbackResistance}
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.reachDistance}

blocks.text: Advanced details

items: The number on a card counts that card alone; the weapon panel is what shows all of the weapon's stats combined - how to read it: [[weapons/weapon_panel]].

items.text: Some stats have a min / max per card; values outside it are clamped to the limit, and the number on the card does not show this - see [[modules/module_limits]].
Some stats have a cap on their combined total; anything above it is lost - see [[modules/module_limits]].

header: Share added to your main-hand weapon

entries.title: Weapon · Damage
entries.summary: Melee, ranged, magic and faction damage

blocks.text: These stats add damage directly: by how you attack (melee, ranged, magic), or against one kind of creature (faction damage).
The first few all go into one <hl>damage pool</hl>: they are added up, then boost the hit together. A hit counts as either melee or ranged, never both.

rows: Melee: you hit the target yourself (swings, sweeps)
Ranged: something you fired hits it (arrows, projectiles, bullets)
Ranged, and the hit is a normal or tipped arrow
Added to the pool along with Ranged Damage
Ranged, and the hit is any other projectile: snowballs, spectral arrows, tridents, gun bullets
Added to the pool along with Ranged Damage
The hit counts as magic damage
<g>Also</g> added to the pool, on top of melee / ranged
Added as is, <w>not</w> multiplied by panel Base Damage; scaled by charge on melee

blocks.text: Once crit chance goes above 100% every hit crits, so {lang:item.module.baseDamageWhenNotCriticalStrike} never applies again.
Faction stats
A faction stat adds damage against one kind of target only. It is its own multiplier, <t>× (1 + value)</t>, applied to both the physical and elemental parts.

rows: "Unknown": the vanilla default type - most mobs
Illagers; <dim>water mobs also fall into this group</dim>

blocks.text: Warframe has the same kind of "+X% damage to one faction" mod, such as Bane of Grineer. The original factions are the Grineer, the Corpus and others; here they become vanilla mob types.
The math
Physical = raw damage × (1 + pool) × panel Base Damage × charge × crit × faction
Elemental = raw damage × element total × panel Base Damage × charge × faction (no crit)
<t>Charge</t>: melee hits are scaled by how far the swing was charged - only a full charge counts as 1, so swinging early costs a lot. Ranged is always 1.

blocks.title: Panel Base Damage below 100%
blocks.text: The weapon panel's {lang:item.module.damage} below 100% is <w>squared</w>: 80% really means 64%, 50% means 25%.
Advanced details

items: Stats resolved on hit (damage, crit, elements, execution...) need a weapon that can hold mods in your main hand; otherwise none of them apply.
Ranged hits use whatever is in your main hand <w>when the hit lands</w>: swap weapons while an arrow is in flight and the new weapon's stats are used.
Negative damage stats on [[start/glossary|Riven mods]] subtract from the pool; at worst the hit deals 0 damage, never negative.

blocks.text: Full calculation order and how magic damage is detected: [[combat/damage]]. Faction damage: [[combat/bane]].
{lang:item.module.first_bullet_damage}, {lang:item.module.gun_damage} and {lang:item.module.headshot_damage} only work on guns - see [[tacz/tacz_gun_attributes]].
{lang:item.module.gun_damage} and {lang:item.module.headshot_damage} only work on guns - see [[tacz/tacz_gun_attributes]].
A crit is a chance to deal multiplied damage. These stats raise your crit chance and crit multiplier.
The panel's {lang:item.module.criticalStrikeProbability} and {lang:item.module.criticalStrikeMultiplier} are both "the weapon's own base value × (1 + stat)". Melee and ranged use separate stats.

rows: Melee crits more often while sprinting
While sprinting, <g>added</g> to melee crit chance before multiplying
Melee crits hit harder with every kill

blocks.text: Crit tiers
Crit chance can go above 100%: past that every hit crits, and the extra is the chance to reach a higher tier.

rows: Always crits; the part above 100% is the chance for tier 2, which is × crit multiplier × 2
At least tier 2; the part above 200% is the chance for tier 3, which is × crit multiplier × 3
Always tier 3; <w>anything higher gives nothing extra</w>
Always crits; the part above 100% is the chance for tier 2, which is × crit multiplier × 2
At least tier 2; the part above 200% is the chance for tier 3, which is × crit multiplier × 3
Always tier 3; <w>anything higher gives nothing extra</w>

blocks.text: Each tier has its own number color (see the table). Non-crits show white numbers, or <c:55FFFF>aqua</c> if the target has a shield.
In Warframe, crit chance can also go past 100% for higher-tier crits. Players name them yellow, orange and red crits after the color of the damage numbers.
Watch out

items: Swinging before your melee attack is fully charged scales crit chance down by the charge: half charged, half the chance. Damage drops even harder: a half-charged swing deals only <w>about a fifth</w> of a full-charge hit - see [[reference/weapon_attr_damage]].
Crits only multiply the <hl>physical part</hl>; elemental damage ignores the crit multiplier (by design).
Once crit chance exceeds 100%, {lang:item.module.baseDamageWhenNotCriticalStrike} can never trigger.

blocks.text: TACZ guns: when one bullet's damage is dealt in two parts, crit is rolled once for each part (by design), and status procs and executions are rolled for each part too. How the damage numbers are shown: [[combat/damage_numbers]].
TACZ guns: when one bullet's damage is dealt in two parts, crit is rolled once for each part (by design), and status procs and executions are rolled for each part too.
Examples and more details: [[combat/crit]].

entries.title: Weapon · Utility
entries.summary: Speed, range, fire rate, multishot, status

blocks.text: These stats do not add damage directly. They make you attack faster, reach further, fire more arrows at once, hit nearby creatures, or proc statuses more often.
<hl>Proc</hl>: a hit has a chance to put an elemental status such as burning or freezing on the target. All statuses: [[combat/element_status]].

rows: Melee reaches further, and sweeps get wider
Added to Attack Range while sprinting
Draw bows and charge up faster
<w>Doubled on bows and crossbows</w>; the math is at the end
The integer part always fires extra; the fraction is a chance for one more
Added to Status Chance while sprinting
Duration and number of DoT ticks × (1 + value)
Ranged hits also hit nearby creatures (splash)
Radius = 1 + value × 2 blocks; each splashed target takes 50% of the main target's final damage

items: Attack Speed and Attack Range only count whole 10% steps and drop the rest; negative Attack Speed slows you in the same steps.
Multishot only works on bows, not crossbows; extra arrows cost no ammo and cannot be picked up.
Above 100% status chance, the integer part always procs and the remainder is a chance for one more. One hit procs at most <t>5</t> times (capped at 500%).

blocks.title: Splash does not pick sides
blocks.text: Every creature in the radius except you and the main target gets hit, pets and villagers included.
Advanced details

items: Fire Rate math: each tick the charge advances extra times equal to the integer part, and the fraction is a chance for one more; doubled on bows and crossbows.
Negative Fire Rate slows charging; at -100% or less you cannot draw at all. Bows and crossbows double it, so -50% is enough.
Using an item that cannot hold mods in your off-hand (eating, drinking, blocking) also follows your main-hand weapon's Fire Rate.
Negative Multishot may cancel the shot.
Sprint Attack Range is checked once per second, so it catches up about 1 s after you start or stop sprinting.
Sprint Status Chance works on ranged attacks too, as long as you are sprinting when you attack.
The panel shows Status Duration as a percent of the base duration.

Splash only deals damage: no status procs, no weapon kill stacks (Warframe kill stacks still count), no execution; the number color copies the main target's crit color. Explosion-type damage never splashes.
At most <t>100</t> status procs happen per tick, counting all players together.

blocks.text: On guns: {lang:item.module.firing_rate} changes the shot interval, {lang:item.module.multishot} adds pellets per shot, and {lang:item.module.bursting_radius} enlarges the gun's own explosion if it has one. Details: [[tacz/tacz_multishot]].
Element stats add elemental damage to every hit, and decide which status the target gets when you proc (burning, freezing, poisoned...).

items: <g>Adds damage</g>: every hit adds elemental damage based on the total of all element stats; crits do not affect it.
<g>Picks the status</g>: on a proc, one status is picked at random, weighted by each element's share - the bigger the value, the likelier.

blocks.text: Elemental = raw damage × element total × panel Base Damage × charge × faction (no crit)
Base elements

rows: Sets the target on fire with damage over time and gradually strips armor (down to -50%)
Slows movement and attack speed, up to 9 stacks (-50% → -90%)
Damage over time; <w>bypasses shields</w> and hits health directly if the target has one

cells: One shock (the lightning is visual only) that paralyzes the target for 0.5 s (nearly frozen)
×1.5 vs undead; ×0.5 if the target has a shield
A proc does nothing: no damage and no paralysis

blocks.text: Physical elements

rows: Bleed: damage over time that hits health directly, ignoring armor and shields
Hurts more if the target has Viral
The target <g>deals</g> -40% damage, -10% more per stack, up to 4 stacks (-70%)
Counts for its melee and anything it shoots; your hits on it are unaffected
Knocks the target back and up

blocks.text: Combined elements
Two base elements combine into one combined element, as shown below.

rows: Leaves a 3-block toxic cloud at the hit point that damages every creature inside <w>except you</w>
Multipliers follow the hit target: ×1.5 vs arthropods, ×0.5 if it has a shield
The target is confused and turns on nearby creatures of its own kind, dealing them +100% damage, up to 10 stacks (max +550%)
Picks the nearest of its kind within 24 blocks, or the nearest creature if none; base duration 12 s
The target takes +100% damage while it has a shield, up to 10 stacks (max +325%)
Strips armor by 26%, up to 10 stacks (max -80%)
Blast damage to the target and every creature within 3 blocks <w>except you</w>
Breaks no blocks; ×1.5 if the target has a shield, otherwise ×0.5
At 10 stacks, max health -50%; also makes Slash bleed hurt more

blocks.text: Combination order

items: Identical elements are merged into one first.
They line up in order of appearance: the [[start/glossary|Kuva weapon]]'s own element comes first, then mods in slot order.
Each base element combines with the first base element before it that is still unpaired and can pair with it.
The three physical elements (Slash, Puncture, Impact) never combine.

blocks.text: So the same three elements can combine differently in a different slot order.
Warframe works the same way: Heat, Cold, Electricity and Toxin pair up into these same six combined elements, and the result also depends on the order of mods on the weapon.
Rules for all statuses

items: Unless noted, statuses last 6 s, and DoTs tick once per second for 6 ticks. Both are extended by {lang:item.module.triggerTime}.
The same DoT does not stack on one target: a new proc keeps the higher per-tick damage and refills the tick count.
Proc damage is based on <t>the hit's physical damage</t> (including crit and faction).

blocks.text: Status damage multipliers
These multipliers only affect damage dealt by procs (DoT / burst), not the elemental damage added to every hit.
Advanced details

items: The status pick only looks at the mods on your main-hand weapon itself.

items.text: The pick uses max-rank values, even if a mod is not fully ranked.

items: Gas and Blast proc damage only counts the two base element stats they are made of: Gas = Heat + Toxin, Blast = Heat + Cold, including the Kuva weapon's own element if it is one of them.
A Gas or Blast stat on a card does <w>not count</w> toward proc damage: with only those, the proc deals no damage; the elemental damage added to every hit is unaffected.

The Electric and Blast hit on the main target gets eaten by vanilla hit invulnerability: only the part above the hit's raw damage gets through, so the number is often small or missing. Creatures caught in the blast around it are unaffected.
The Gas cloud fades about 1 s after the hit target dies.
Faction damage applies <w>squared</w> to status proc damage (by design).
[[start/glossary|Riven mods]] never roll combined elements; only mods with fixed stats have them.

blocks.text: Full numbers for every status: [[combat/element_status]].
These stats can kill a target outright when its health is low enough or its luck runs out, or strip away its buffs.

rows: Low enough health: the target is executed
Health <w>before</w> the hit ≤ max health × value
Each hit has a chance to execute the target, whatever its health
Chance = value, rolled only if the threshold did not trigger; very small values, shown with three decimals
Removes random beneficial potion effects from the target on hit (debuffs untouched)
Integer part = guaranteed removals; fraction = chance to remove one more

blocks.text: Example: {lang:item.module.purge_buff} 150% → removes 1 for sure, plus a 50% chance to remove another

items: Executions happen <t>1</t> tick after the hit: threshold executions release soul particles, chance kills release crit sparks.
Only checked on direct hits from a weapon that can hold mods: each Multishot arrow rolls separately, while splash and status DoTs never roll.
An execution counts as a kill: +1 weapon [[reference/weapon_attr_killstack|kill stack]] (but no Warframe kill stack).

blocks.text: Advanced details

items: This mod gives bosses no exemption, so the [[start/glossary|Kuva Lich]] (this mod's boss) can be executed; other mods' bosses with health locks or revives may not be.
[[start/glossary|Riven mods]] never roll these three as negative stats.

blocks.text: {lang:item.module.true_bullet} and {lang:item.module.gun_loot_drop} only work with gun bullets - see [[tacz/tacz_gun_attributes]].

entries.title: Weapon · Kill Stacks
entries.summary: Kill stacks: stronger with every kill

blocks.text: Stats whose card says "gained on kill" stack up: every target you kill with a weapon that can hold mods adds +1 stack, and more stacks mean a bigger bonus.

rows: Value per stack × stacks, up to the cap
When the timer runs out without a kill you lose <t>1</t> stack, then the timer restarts
Cleared when you log out; <g>not cleared on death</g>

blocks.text: In the table, "+value" means each stack adds that value to the stat of the same name.

rows: Damage +value × number of <w>harmful potion effects</w> on the target; added to the damage pool, melee and ranged
Melee crit multiplier × (1 + value × stacks), a <w>separate multiplier</w>
{lang:item.module.firing_rate} +value, also doubled on bows and crossbows

items: Stacks are stored on you per stat type, not on the weapon: swapping weapons keeps them, but they only apply while your current weapon's panel has that stat.
{lang:item.module.killStackBaseDamage} only counts <w>potion-type</w> debuffs (Slowness, Poison, Weakness...); this mod's element statuses are not potion effects and do not count.
Only a kill by the weapon hit itself counts; kills by status DoTs or splash do not. Executions count as a kill.

blocks.text: Warframe's Galvanized mods work like this: a kill grants a bonus for a while, and the bonus can stack several times.

blocks.title: Advanced details
blocks.text: Whether a hit killed is judged on the damage before armor, so now and then a hit that fails to kill still adds a stack.
Full kill stack mechanics: [[combat/kill_stack]]. Reading your current stacks on the panel: [[weapons/weapon_panel]].
[[start/glossary|Warframe mods]] are mods for yourself, installed in the [[warframe/warframe_table]] (<t>8</t> slots). These stats cover your health, armor and shields.

rows: Each full 10% → +10%; negative values bottom out at -90%
Each full 10% → both +10%; negative values lower them in the same steps

cells: Gives you a shield that takes hits first
Gives no yellow hearts, and while equipped it wipes those from golden apples and the like
They only survive during the wait after you take a hit or land one
Recharges shield cap × 1% × (1 + value) per second; additive across mods
How long before shields start recharging
<w>Multiplies per mod</w>: about 10 s × (1 + value) × (1 + value)...; negative values shorten it

blocks.text: How shields recharge
<hl>Shields</hl> are vanilla absorption (yellow hearts), used up before your health. Recharging goes in three steps:

items: When you <w>take a hit or land one</w>, shield recharge goes on hold: about 10 s × the delay multiplier (rounded down to whole seconds).
If your shield is empty after that hit, the wait is ×3.
After the wait, shields recharge once per second until full.

blocks.text: Advanced details

items: Warframe stats refresh about every 0.25 s.

items.text: Yellow hearts from golden apples and the like are trimmed down to your shield cap.

blocks.text: <dim>The three "Fixed" stats below never appear on built-in mods or [[start/glossary|Riven mods]]; they only come from custom mods added to the modpack.</dim>

rows: Max health is <w>set</w> to this number; additive across mods; percent Health stops working
Armor is set to this number; additive across mods; armor from worn gear and percent Armor stop mattering
Shield cap is set to this number; additive across mods; percent Shield stops working

blocks.text: Shield details: [[warframe/shield]]. Why health and armor only count whole 10% steps: [[reference/attr_rules]].
These [[start/glossary|Warframe]] stats make you take less of one kind of damage, get knocked back less, or heal more.

rows: Less lightning damage (lightning strikes, the Electric element)
Each full 10% → knockback resistance +0.1; additive across mods
More healing (natural regen, Regeneration, Instant Health...)

blocks.text: Example: two 60% Fire Resistance mods → damage × 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, an 84% reduction (not 120%)

items: Multiplying gives diminishing returns: full immunity needs a single 100% mod (or the kill stack version reaching value × stacks = 100%).
At 100% knockback resistance you take no knockback at all.
Negative resistance makes you take more damage; at a healing total of -100% or less you cannot heal at all.

blocks.text: Resistances only reduce the damage that <w>gets through your shield</w> to your health; whatever the shield absorbs is not reduced.

blocks.title: Advanced details
blocks.text: Other mods' "electric" damage does not necessarily count as lightning.
Kill stack versions of the resistances: [[reference/warframe_attr_killstack]].
These [[start/glossary|Warframe]] stats cover everyday abilities: how fast you run, how high you jump, how far you reach and how fast you mine.

rows: Move faster; called sprint, but <w>walking gets it too</w>
Height is about (1 + value) times normal

items: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.reachDistance} does not affect hitting mobs - that is the weapon's {lang:item.module.attackRange}.

items.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.oreDropMultiplier} only works on ores you mine yourself, and Silk Touch never benefits. Details: [[world/ore_drop_multiplier]].

blocks.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.itemDropMultiplier}

items: Only kills credited to you count: melee, arrows and guns all work, pet kills do not.
Only animals and "monster"-class mobs are affected.
Gear, weapons and tools (anything with durability) are never multiplied.
Fractions of an item round up by chance; at a total multiplier of 0 or less, all non-gear drops disappear.

blocks.text: On gun kills, your gun's {lang:item.module.gun_loot_drop} is added to this stat - see [[tacz/tacz_gun_attributes]].
Advanced details

items: Jump math: jump velocity × √(1 + value).

items.text: Slimes, magma cubes, ghasts, phantoms, shulkers, the Ender Dragon, and water mobs such as fish and squid are neither animals nor monsters in vanilla, so their drops are not multiplied. NPCs from the Custom NPCs mod are an exception and do count.
The drop multiplier has no cap; anything over a stack drops as several piles.
Other mods' drop bonuses in the pack are applied first and this one multiplies last, so they compound.

entries.title: Warframe · Kill Stacks
entries.summary: Kill stacks: tougher with every kill

blocks.text: [[start/glossary|Warframe]] stats whose card says "gained on kill" stack up: every target you kill adds +1 stack, making you tougher the longer you fight.

rows: Damage credited to you finishes off the target: melee, arrows and guns all count
When the timer runs out without a kill you lose <t>1</t> stack, then the timer restarts
Cleared when you log out; <g>not cleared on death</g>

blocks.text: In the table, "+value" means each stack adds that value to the normal stat of the same name.

cells: Shield recharge wait × (1 + value × stacks), its own multiplier

rows: Fire damage taken × (1 − value × stacks), its own multiplier
Lightning damage taken × (1 − value × stacks), its own multiplier
Player damage taken × (1 − value × stacks), its own multiplier

items: Kills by pets, status DoTs or executions / instant kills do not count; kills by weapon splash do.
Stacks are stored on you: they stop applying when you remove the mod, and whatever stacks remain count again when you put it back.
The kill stack version shares its name with the normal stat; the one whose card says "gained on kill" is the stacking version.

blocks.text: Kill stack mechanics: [[combat/kill_stack]]. Normal versions: [[reference/warframe_attr_survival]], [[reference/warframe_attr_resist]].
